text: Explain how a bill becomes an Act of Parliament. Assess the effectiveness of this process for
creating law. [25]
Johann has been arrested and charged with three counts of assault. He is 42 and has previously
been convicted of theft. He has a wife and three children under the age of eight who live with him
in a rented flat. He has a job as a mechanic in a local garage. He also has family in Australia.
Explain which factors will be considered when deciding whether or not to grant bail to Johann.
Justify whether it is ever appropriate to grant bail to someone charged with an offence. [25]
Explain three types of delegated legislation. Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of this
form of law-making. [25]
In both the Magistrates’ Court and the Crown Court, laypeople are used to make decisions.
Explain the role of both the jury and the lay magistrate in criminal cases. Assess the extent to
which it is appropriate to use non-qualified people for these roles. [25]
Explain the various forms of alternative dispute resolution (ADR). Evaluate the advantages and
disadvantages of each. [25]
Describe the structure and role of the Crown Prosecution Service. Assess the extent to which it
has been successful in preventing miscarriages of justice. [25]
